tagline: A leading Italian insurance group focused on sustainable growth and customer-centric solutions
hero_kpi_rationale: The operating margin of 12.4% reflects the group's operational discipline and its ability to generate profitability despite a fragile macroeconomic environment. This is the most revealing KPI of an insurer's operational health.

kpis.name: Operating margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenues, measuring current profitability.
kpis.description: Operating margin is improving thanks to good control of overhead costs and integration of group entities.
kpis.signal: Improvement in operational discipline and group synergies.

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenues and direct costs, expressed as a percentage of revenues.
kpis.description: Gross margin is improving slightly in 2024, supported by rigorous claims management and optimization of operating costs.
kpis.signal: Stability and slight improvement in gross margin despite a fragile macroeconomic environment.

kpis.name: R&D investments (% revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development spending relative to revenues.
kpis.description: R&D investments remain limited, focused on improving digital customer tools and cybersecurity.
kpis.signal: Low R&D intensity, consistent with a traditional insurance model.

kpis.name: Investments
kpis.explanation: Spending on tangible and intangible assets to support operations.
kpis.description: Investments focus primarily on information systems and digital customer platforms.
kpis.signal: Moderate CAPEX, focused on digitalization and operational efficiency.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the group.
kpis.description: The group maintains a headcount rationalization policy while strengthening digital skills.
kpis.signal: Slight reduction in headcount despite rising productivity.

kpis.name: Dividend per share
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 0.85 EUR in latest year.

kpis.name: Capital returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 0.953 Bn EUR in latest year.

kpis.name: Payout ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio: Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 64.3% in latest year.

risks.title: Risk of partial internal model
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned early in report with neutral technical language ('plan for extension'). Trend stable, partial model in place since 2016. High-weight regulatory category as it depends on IVASS approval for Solvency II compliance.

risks.title: Risk of credit concentration
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned mid-report with technical language ('concentration risk are assessed'). Trend stable, integrated into existing internal model. High-weight credit category for an insurer exposed to banking counterparties and bonds.

risks.title: Risk of catastrophe underwriting risk
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned early in report with explicit mention ('catastrophe risk'). Trend stable but language indicates specific measures for earthquakes. High-weight industrial category for non-life insurer exposed to natural events.

risks.title: Risk of personal data compliance
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned mid-report with prescriptive language ('requires continuous training'). Trend stable with continuous DPO controls. High-weight regulatory category as GDPR imposes strict obligations with substantial penalties.

risks.title: Risk of employee turnover and talent retention
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned mid-report with factual data (120 departures, 270 entries). Trend stable with voluntary early retirement agreement signed in 2022. Moderate-weight key person category as insurer depends on technical skills but has training programs.

risks.title: Risk of technology dependence
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned mid-report with strategic importance language ('key asset', 'continuously enhanced'). Trend up with increased ICT investments and Leitha creation in 2016. High-weight technology category as predictive models and AI are critical for pricing and claims.

risks.title: Risk of reputation and crisis management
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned late in report with strategic importance language ('strategic asset', 'credibility and reliability essential'). Trend stable with reputation management program since 2014. High-weight reputation category for insurer where trust is fundamental.

ai_positioning.summary: Unipol adopts a cautious approach to artificial intelligence, using it primarily for back-office process automation and claims management improvement. AI is not yet a major strategic lever.
evidence: Limited deployment of AI tools for claims management
Absence of mention of transformative AI initiatives in the annual report
